page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-2xL4 is a GPU-accelerated server configured with an AMD EPYC 9575F processor featuring 12 physical cores and 12 vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB per core. Graphics and parallel processing acceleration are delivered via two NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined 48 GB of VRAM. This server operates on the KVM hypervisor and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address, but features no local storage.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in single-core operations, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance scoring 3942.28 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 42.79 GB/sec. Text generation for small language models (135M) also falls into the top tier at 349.81 tokens/sec. Conversely, multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average tier. For instance, stress-ng multi-core CPU performance scored 45719.52, and large-block memory read bandwidth reached 146.11 GB/sec.

A primary architectural tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which may introduce resource contention compared to dedicated CPU instances. Additionally, the complete lack of local storage requires external storage attachments for persistent data. Given the dual NVIDIA L4 GPUs and 128 GB of RAM, this server is optimized for GPU-accelerated workloads such as small-scale LLM inference, machine learning model training, and parallel data processing, while being less suited for disk-heavy database operations without external storage.
